summary: BLM former lookout site 18 miles northwest of Vale, Oregon: a 1960s cab, staffed in the 1965-67 clippings, now gone.

facts.status_note: Both listings say the cab is now gone; no source describes what remains on the ground.

events.note: Sources give only the 1960s (Built: 1960's). Year 1960 is a placeholder for that decade, not a sourced year; see corrections.
Earliest season in the newspaper items quoted on the Rex's page. Not a confirmed first year of staffing.
Latest season mentioned, August 1967. Not a confirmed last year of staffing.

evidence.supports: A cab was built on the site in the 1960s and is now gone.
evidence.quote: A cab was built on the site in the 1960's and is now gone.

evidence.supports: The Bureau of Land Management administers the land.
The site lies about 18 miles northwest of Vale.
The site lies in Malheur County, Oregon.
One listing gives the elevation as 6,482 feet.
The other listing gives the elevation as 5,400 feet.
The August 1965 item says two Burnt River Valley girls manned the lookout that summer.
evidence.quote: This summer it is being manned by two Burnt River Valley girls.

evidence.supports: Wilma Morgan was the official lookout, with Margie Elliott as assistant.
evidence.quote: They are Wilma Morgan, official lookout and Margie Elliott, assistant lookout.

evidence.supports: Water was trucked in from Vale.
evidence.quote: Their water is trucked to them from Vale.

evidence.supports: A battery-powered shortwave radio was the girls' one tie to the wider world.
evidence.quote: The girls have a battery-powered, transistorized shortwave radio being their only link with the 'outside world.'

evidence.supports: Wilma and Ruth Morgan were at the lookout in August 1967.
evidence.quote: Ruth Morgan and Wilma Morgan were home from the lookout this weekend.

evidence.supports: Wilma and Ruth Morgan were at the lookout in summer 1966.
evidence.quote: Wilma and Ruth Morgan are at Cottonwood Lookout this summer.

corrections.why: The FFLOS page gives Built as 1960's and says a cab was built on the site in the 1960's. Neither listing gives 1960 as the year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The clippings on the Rex's page spell the assistant's name Margie, Margy, Marjorie and Marjie Elliott. The story uses Margie Elliott from the August 1965 item.

notes_for_editor: Fact-checked 2026-10-09. check_quotes.py found all 13 evidence quotes in the cached sources on its first run. Story claims were re-checked against the three pages: firetower.org (Administered by Bureau of Land Management; Built 1960's; Elevation 6,482 ft), firelookout.com (Bureau of Land Management; 18 miles northwest of Vale; Elevation 5400') and the Rex's page items of June 1965 to August 1967. Elevation conflict (6,482 ft vs 5400 ft) is unresolved and the story omits the figure. The FFLOS registration date (November 1, 2019) is on firetower.org but the story does not use it. Staffing evidence comes from newspaper items as transcribed on the Rex's page, not from the originals, and the assistant's name is spelled several ways there. No source describes access or what remains on the site. Confidence stays medium: staffing rests on transcriptions and the built year is decade-only.
